chapter: Philadelphia, New York and Sam Wooding in Europe
title: Wooding as a descriptive arranger
summary: The band played classics and Wooding wrote effects pieces such as the Railroad Train and a radio sketch.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, wasn't -- was the band, at that time, playing things -- some of the classics?

He was one of the greatest descriptive arrangers that I have ever ran into. We had a thing called the "Railroad Train." That he wrote, and you could actually hear the trains coming, he had all kinds of effects on the bandstand. That's why that man was so famous.
And he had like a radio thing he did. All announcement static with the static and everything and he was one of the greatest writers, I think I ever ran into.
So he had a lot of imagination?
